name: Server Manager
description: Remote server management for Joinery instances
author: Joinery

settingsGroups.services: Joinery-run services (mail and backup storage tenants)

settings.name: server_manager_provisioning_admin_alert_email
settings.label: Provisioning alert email
settings.helptext: Who to tell when a customer provisioning job needs attention.

settings.name: server_manager_provisioning_domain_question_id
settings.label: Domain question id
settings.helptext: The purchase question whose answer supplies the customer's domain.

settings.name: server_manager_log_excerpt_retention_days
settings.label: Days to keep log excerpts read from nodes
settings.helptext: A site_log or log_table_tail job brings back a redacted excerpt of a node's own logs. After this many days the excerpt is blanked and the job row is kept as the record that it ran. 0 keeps every excerpt.

settings.name: server_manager_cert_expiry_warn_days
settings.label: Warn this many days before a certificate expires
settings.helptext: The safety net. A node's certificate is watched on the node's own address whether or not an edge fronts the name, and renewal more than a day overdue alerts on its own, before this threshold is reached.

settings.name: server_manager_linode_referral_url
settings.helptext: Linode referral URL shown on the Connect page's create-account link. New accounts signed up through it receive Linode's referral credit.
settings.label: Linode referral URL

settings.name: server_manager_customer_cloud_region
settings.helptext: Default region for customer-cloud instances.
settings.label: Customer cloud region

settings.name: server_manager_customer_cloud_type
settings.helptext: Default instance type for customer-cloud instances.
settings.label: Customer cloud instance type

settings.name: server_manager_customer_cloud_image
settings.helptext: OS image for customer-cloud instances. Must be an Ubuntu LTS the installer supports (26.04 or 24.04).
settings.label: Customer cloud image

settings.name: server_manager_hosted_regions
settings.label: Regions a buyer may choose
settings.helptext: Space-separated Linode region ids offered on the Managed configure page. Empty means the one region in Customer cloud region, and the field does not render.

settings.name: server_manager_draft_days
settings.label: Days a site draft is kept
settings.helptext: A Managed site draft the buyer never continued is deleted after this many days; one frozen for the cart but never paid returns to draft, because its domain quote is stale.

settings.name: server_manager_upgrade_retention_count
settings.helptext: How many recent core upgrade archives to keep on disk. Older archives are removed after each publish; their release-history records are always kept. Archives marked Keep, and any version a managed node is running, are never removed. Set to 0 to keep every archive.
settings.label: Upgrade archives to keep

settings.name: server_manager_agent_source_path
settings.helptext: Path to the joinery-agent source checkout on this management node. When set (or when the default /home/user1/joinery-agent exists), publishing a release rebuilds and signs the bundled agent artifact; otherwise the previously bundled artifact carries forward.
settings.label: Agent source path

messages.pattern: An absolute path made of letters, digits, dots, _ and -.

settings.name: server_manager_fleet_backup_enabled
settings.label: Back up newly managed nodes by default
settings.helptext: Whether a node this management node manages gets backed up here unless someone says otherwise. On by default, and that default is what stops a new node being forgotten. A site's own backups are separate and unaffected either way.

settings.name: server_manager_fleet_backup_window_start
settings.label: Backup window starts (UTC)
settings.helptext: The earliest a fleet backup begins. Each node gets its own minute inside the window, derived from its name, so they do not all start at once.

settings.name: server_manager_fleet_backup_window_minutes
settings.label: Backup window length (minutes)
settings.helptext: How wide to spread node start times. Wider means fewer simultaneous uploads and a longer tail; 120 suits a few dozen nodes.

settings.name: server_manager_fleet_backup_mode
settings.label: How fleet backups are taken
settings.helptext: Incremental chains send only what changed after the first run — measured at 193 MB then 37 kB — which across a fleet is most of the bandwidth. A full every time makes each restore point self-contained at much greater cost.

settings.name: server_manager_fleet_backup_keep_days
settings.label: Fewest days of backups kept per node
settings.helptext: Each site chooses how many days of backups it keeps, on its own Backups page, and this node deletes its copies of that site by that choice. This is the floor under it: however short a site sets its window, backups younger than this are never deleted from here — so an intruder on a site cannot shorten the window to erase its history.

settings.name: server_manager_fleet_backup_full_interval_days
settings.label: Days before a chain starts a fresh full
settings.helptext: How long one chain runs before the next backup starts over with a full. Shorter means more storage and shorter restore chains.

settings.name: server_manager_fleet_backup_verify_every_days
settings.label: Days between backup verifications (0 = never)
settings.helptext: How often each node's newest backup is verified restorable by opening and reading it on the node: every archive it depends on is downloaded from backup storage, decrypted with the node's own key and read to the end, then removed. Nothing on the site is touched. Each verification downloads the whole set once, so on metered storage it is that much egress per node per interval.

settings.name: server_manager_fleet_backup_max_concurrent
settings.label: Backups running at once across the fleet
settings.helptext: A ceiling on simultaneous fleet backups. Nodes over the limit wait for the next tick rather than queueing.

settings.name: server_manager_namecheap_api_user
settings.label: Namecheap API user
settings.helptext: The Namecheap account username the API calls are made as.

settings.name: server_manager_namecheap_api_key
settings.label: Namecheap API key
settings.helptext: Set this on the Provisioning Setup page, which seals it at rest.

settings.name: server_manager_namecheap_client_ip
settings.label: Allowlisted client IP
settings.helptext: The management node's egress IP, allowlisted in the Namecheap API panel.

settings.name: server_manager_namecheap_sandbox
settings.label: Use Namecheap sandbox
settings.helptext: Point registrar calls at Namecheap's sandbox. Names bought there are not real.

settings.name: server_manager_domain_tlds
settings.label: Offered TLDs
settings.helptext: Space-separated. A domain outside these endings is refused at checkout.

settings.name: server_manager_namecheap_promotion_code
settings.label: Namecheap promotion code
settings.helptext: A registrar coupon applied to every domain quote and every registration alike, so the buyer pays what the registrar charges. Set it on the Provisioning Setup page, which seals it at rest. Empty means no coupon.

settings.name: server_manager_domain_orphan_swept_id
settings.helptext: High-water mark over order items already checked for a paid domain year that produced no registration. Written by ManagedDomainWatch so each such order is reported once.

settings.name: server_manager_operator_cloud_token
settings.label: Operator cloud token
settings.helptext: The Linode personal access token (scope linodes:read_write) hosted instances are created on. Set it on the Provisioning Setup page, which seals it at rest. It stays on this management node and never reaches a machine this plane creates.

settings.name: server_manager_smtp2go_api_key
settings.label: SMTP2GO master API key
settings.helptext: The master key every hosted customer's subaccount is administered with. Set it on the Provisioning Setup page, which seals it at rest. Only a per-customer SMTP user ever reaches a customer's box.

settings.name: server_manager_smtp2go_sandbox_users
settings.label: Sandbox the SMTP users this plane mints
settings.helptext: Every customer SMTP user is created in SMTP2GO's sandbox status: mail through it is accepted and counted but never delivered. For a rehearsal plane, so a site built to prove the pipeline can email nobody. Leave off on a plane that hosts real customers.

settings.name: server_manager_smtp2go_webhook_secret
settings.label: SMTP2GO webhook secret
settings.helptext: The basic-auth password this plane requires on the SMTP2GO event webhook. SMTP2GO does not sign its webhooks, so this plus the provider's own address range is the whole check — and webhook counts only ever move a banner, never a cap.

settings.name: server_manager_hosted_send_allowance
settings.label: Sends per month, per customer
settings.helptext: Set as the monthly limit on every hosted customer's SMTP2GO subaccount, at creation and whenever this changes. The provider counts and enforces it; the platform is not in the send path.

settings.name: server_manager_hosted_shelf_allowance_gb
settings.label: Backup storage per customer (GB)
settings.helptext: How much of the fleet's backup storage a hosted customer's backups may occupy before their runs stop. Measured from the listing the retention pass already takes.

settings.name: server_manager_hosted_trial_days
settings.label: Free trial length (days, 0 for none)
settings.helptext: How long hosting is free before the subscription starts charging. Zero means there is no trial: hosting is billed from checkout and a new site opens as subscribed. With a trial, the trial itself is the Stripe subscription's own trial period, set on the product; this is what the site's banner counts down when no subscription date is known yet, and it must match.

settings.name: server_manager_hosted_grace_days
settings.label: Grace after a failed payment (days)
settings.helptext: How long a hosted site keeps running after a charge fails. At the end the instance is shut down by API and a deletion task is raised for a person — the platform never deletes a cloud instance itself.

settings.name: server_manager_hosted_shelf_days
settings.label: Backup storage kept after non-payment (days)
settings.helptext: How long a shut-down customer's backups stay in backup storage before the retention pass prunes them. Counted from the failed payment, not the shutdown.

settings.name: server_manager_hosted_manage_url
settings.label: Where customers manage their hosting
settings.helptext: The https address of the buyer's own sites page on the store — pushed to each hosted site's banner as its Manage hosting link. Usually https://<store>/profile/server_manager.

settings.name: server_manager_smtp2go_referral_url
settings.label: SMTP2GO referral URL
settings.helptext: Where a customer who outgrows the send allowance opens their own SMTP2GO account. Shown on their banner only when that allowance is near.

settings.name: server_manager_storage_referral_url
settings.label: Backup storage referral URL
settings.helptext: Where a customer who outgrows its backup storage opens their own bucket. Shown on their banner only when that allowance is near.

settings.name: server_manager_hosted_transfer_alerted_time
settings.helptext: When the operator was last told the account's outbound transfer pool passed 80%. Written by the hosted watch so one alert is sent per billing period, not one per tick.

settings.name: server_manager_services_grace_days
settings.label: Services grace after the paid-through date (days)
settings.helptext: How long a self-hosted site keeps using our outbound mail and backup storage after its paid-through date passes. At the end mail's subaccount is closed and the backup storage broker refuses the site; backup storage is kept 90 days from that day and then pruned. Blank means 14.

settings.name: server_manager_services_shelf_target_id
settings.label: Backup storage target
settings.helptext: The id of the backup target row whose bucket is the services backup storage: the broker signs every tenant upload against that row's credential, and each tenant lives under its own prefix inside it. Blank means the one enabled target, which is the answer on a plane with exactly one.

settings.name: server_manager_services_shelf_keep_chains
settings.label: Backup storage restore points kept per site
settings.helptext: How many backup chains (restore points) the plane keeps in backup storage for each tenant site, per profile. Older chains are pruned whole by the reconcile; a chain still being written is never touched. Blank means 4.

sealed_secrets.label: Clone export key armed on a provision's source
Managed site draft's domain registrant contact

hosted.deletion_required.label: Hosted instance needs deleting by a person
hosted.deletion_required.description: A hosted site's grace period ran out. The platform has powered its instance off — the strongest thing it does on its own — and somebody has to delete it at the provider to stop the bill.

payload.shelf_ends_time: When this customer's backups are pruned (UTC)

notify.body_template: Hosting for {domain} ended unpaid. Instance {instance_id} is powered off and still billing until somebody deletes it at the provider. Their backups are kept until {shelf_ends_time}.

hosted.transfer_pool_high.label: Cloud transfer pool is nearly used up
hosted.transfer_pool_high.description: The operator's account-wide outbound transfer allowance passed its warning mark. Transfer is pooled across the account, so there is no per-customer number and no per-customer action — this is one look, not an alarm per site.

notify.body_template: {used_gb} GB of the account's {quota_gb} GB outbound transfer pool is used this period. Overage is billed per gigabyte.
